source_text: Gratia - inquit - ex multis delictis in iustificationem [n155] ; tu parvulos non plus quam uni obnoxios dicis esse peccato. Vides ergo in eorum persona laudem gratiae claudicantem, quia non invenit multa peccata, quorum remissione laudetur; quod dixit itaque apostolus Paulus: Gratia autem ex multis delictis in iustificationem [n156] , falsissimum esse in parvulorum statu proditur. Quo hinc tu igitur conaberis exsilire? Procul dubio dicturus es, hunc enim sensum tuum superior sermo patefecit, hoc, quod ait Apostolus: Gratia autem ex multis delictis in iustificationem [n157] , apud homines perfectae aetatis impleri, qui multis delictis per motum propriae voluntatis convincantur obnoxii, in parvulis autem non ex multis, sed ex uno delicto fieri iustificationem.
pass_a_gloss: Grace, he says, from many offenses into justification; you say that little children are liable to not more than one sin. You see therefore in their person the praise of grace limping, because it does not find many sins by whose remission it may be praised; what therefore the apostle Paul said: But grace from many offenses into justification, is betrayed as most false in the state of little children. Whither therefore will you try to leap out from here? Beyond doubt you are about to say, for the earlier speech opened this sense of yours, that this, which the Apostle says: But grace from many offenses into justification, is fulfilled among human beings of perfect age, who are convicted as liable to many offenses through a motion of proper will, but in little children justification is made not from many, but from one offense.

LS iustificatio; Blaise forensic making-just, not later system

pass_b_english: ‘Grace,’ he says, ‘is from many offenses to justification’ (Romans 5:16). You say infants are liable for no more than one sin. You therefore see praise of grace limping in their case, because it finds no multitude of sins whose forgiveness can earn it praise. Consequently, the apostle Paul’s words, ‘But grace is from many offenses to justification’ (Romans 5:16), are exposed as utterly false in infants’ condition. Where will you try to jump from here? No doubt you will say—for your previous argument has disclosed this intention—that the apostle’s statement, ‘But grace is from many offenses to justification’ (Romans 5:16), is fulfilled in adults, who are proved liable for many offenses through the movement of their own will; but that in infants justification comes not from many offenses but from one.

choices.why: Paul's delictum of the one man; an act, not a nature.
Paul's iustificatio vitae; keep forensic making-just, not a later systematic slogan as default.
